answer: Countersign-graph community detection prunes sybil clusters before they cash out. Picture trust as sparrows feeding across a city: genuine agents perch in scattered gardens, while a bot farm huddles on a single branch, every trust edge pointing inward. Auditors flag dense, inward-only cliques that never reach outside nodes - a pearl sealed in a closed shell stays a pearl, but earns no light. Reputation only counts when it climbs toward the zenith of graph centrality, bridging diverse clusters no farmer can fake at scale.
